neighbours.label: a connective that turns to reinforce or contradict the preceding clause ('in fact', 'to the contrary', 'so ... that')
fire: The minister denied any delay. In fact, the project is a year behind.
Critics said the film would flop; on the contrary, it broke records.
The soup was so salty that nobody could finish it.
He was not angry at all. In fact, he seemed relieved.
The storm was so loud that the children could not sleep.
The rumours were false; to the contrary, the firm is hiring.
Sales did not fall last year. In fact, they rose by a fifth.
The hill was so steep that we had to push our bikes.
quiet: The minister spoke about the project at a press event.
Critics watched the film at a festival in the spring.
The soup had carrots, onions and a little salt.
He walked home and made a cup of tea.
The storm brought rain and wind to the coast.
The firm makes chairs, tables and shelves.
Sales were reported in the spring and in the autumn.
We rode our bikes up the hill and down the other side.

predictions: Fires on 'fact' in 'in fact', 'contrary' in 'on/to the contrary' and 'that' after 'so ADJ'; quiet on plain additive sentences.
notes: Broad pole. Probe: 'to the contrary' 0.528, 'In fact' 0.529, 'so vile that' 0.398, clause 'and planned' 0.272; plain lists 'and waved flags' 0.103, 'cat and dog' 0.029.
